summary: A command that saves one of a course's files to a local file. internal/client/download.go is hand-authored and holds both requests: GET /api/v1/courses/{course_id}/files/{file_id} for the file's record, which says where its contents are, and a streaming GET of that address for the bytes. internal/cli/download.go is the command: download <file_id> with --output, --course and --force, printing {"action":"download","file":{...},"saved_to":...,"bytes":...}. --output takes either a folder, in which case the file keeps the name Canvas has for it, or the name to save it under. root.go gains the AddCommand line in the hand-authored block, and the command carries a pp:path annotation of /api/v1/courses/{course_id}/files/{file_id} so Canvas Builder's untraceable-command hiding (sandbox-command-surface) keeps it visible by rule. internal/sandbox/messages.go gains MsgNotAFileAddress. internal/gatewaytest/fake.go gains Truncated, which answers with a Content-Length larger than the body it sends and then closes the connection. upload.go's uploadTimeout is now transferTimeout, with minUploadRate renamed to match, because the download needs the same bound for the same reason. --dry-run shows the first of the two requests and stops, because the second's address is in the answer the dry run never gets.
reason:
An agent remediating a document, or reading a file before replacing it, needs the file itself, and this is the only way it gets one. Two things about it are particular, and both come from the same fact: the address the bytes come from is named by Canvas, not composed by this CLI, and Canvas's copy of a file record is something an agent can write to.

So that address is checked twice before it is dialed. Once by the client's general rule, which refuses anything that isn't Canvas Builder's gateway, and once by a rule of its own: the path has to be a file download, /files/<id>/download or /courses/<id>/files/<id>/download. An address on the gateway that isn't a file download is still an address this CLI would fetch with its token on Canvas's word, and a file's url is the one place Canvas gets to say where that token goes. A hop is checked by the client's existing CheckRedirect, so a file address that answers with somewhere else gets no further than the check.

The file record is read with GetNoCache. A file's address carries a verifier that expires, so a remembered record sends the fetch at a dead address.

Nothing is written under the name the agent asked for until the whole file has arrived. The bytes go to a temporary name in the target folder and are renamed once the size Canvas stated has been matched; a download that stops partway leaves nothing behind. Half a file under the right name is worse than no file, because the next command reads it and reports what isn't there. A body that stops short is MsgDownloadShort, and the error carries how many bytes of how many arrived.

In Canvas Builder the target passes sandbox.Inside before anything is asked of Canvas, so a file that may not be saved is never fetched, and --course defaults to the course the folder belongs to. The name taken from Canvas is reduced to a base name, so a display_name of "../../evil.sh" saves as evil.sh in the folder that was asked for.
known_limitations:
download does not appear in `which` yet. whichIndex is generated and the curated capability index is Task 11's work, so for now the command is found through --help.

A file whose record states no size (size 0, or absent) can't be checked against what arrived; io.Copy's own error is the only signal there is, and a server that closes cleanly after half a body with no declared length would be read as a whole file. Canvas states a size for every file it holds, so this is a gap in what the check can see rather than one in what Canvas sends.

More bytes than the record says is reported as its own error rather than as a short download, and nothing is saved. That is the right outcome, but it means a file Canvas has grown since the record was read fails rather than being saved under its new size.

The folder --output names has to exist, and a missing one is exit 2 naming the folder. Creating it would mean a typo in a path becomes a folder in the instructor's course workspace, named after the typo.

The check that nothing is in the way runs before the rename, so a file that appears in that gap is replaced without --force. Closing the window entirely needs an atomic create-and-rename the standard library doesn't offer, and the only writer in a course workspace is the agent itself.

"." and ".." are refused as --output, as Plan E asks, even though in Canvas Builder "." would resolve to a real folder: a folder named by where the command happens to be standing isn't a place to put a course's file.

--dry-run can only show the first request. The second one's address, and the file's name when --output named a folder, are both in the answer to the first, so the dry run's envelope reports where the file would have gone rather than the name it would have had.
validated_outcome:
go build ./... and go vet ./... clean. go test ./... passing across every package on darwin/arm64 with Go 1.27.1, exit 0. go test -race ./internal/client/ ./internal/cli/ ./internal/sandbox/ passing. golangci-lint run --max-issues-per-linter=0 --max-same-issues=0 reports nothing on internal/client/download.go, internal/cli/download.go, either test file, internal/sandbox/messages.go or internal/gatewaytest/fake.go; the touched generated file reports only its pre-existing findings. gofmt -l clean on every file in this patch.

New coverage. internal/client/download_test.go: TestDownloadFileSavesWhatCanvasSent asserts the bytes are the file, that the fetch kept the verifier Canvas put in the address, and that it carried the token in a header rather than the query. TestDownloadFileRefusesURLOffGateway points the file's url at a second local server and asserts a RefusedError naming Canvas Builder's address, with that server seeing no connection and nothing written. TestDownloadFileRefusesURLThatIsntAFile points it at an API path on the gateway itself and asserts a refusal with that path never fetched. TestDownloadFileFollowsGatewayRedirectOnly covers both hops: one within Canvas Builder, where the bytes arrive, and one out of it, which is refused with the other server seeing nothing. TestDownloadFileShortBodyIsShort declares 2,048 bytes, sends 1,024 and closes, and asserts the error says the download stopped before the whole file arrived.

internal/cli/download_test.go, through runCLI against the fake: TestDownloadSavesFile asserts the two requests in order, the same Authorization on both, no token in either query, the download query left exactly as Canvas wrote it, and the printed envelope's file, saved_to and bytes. TestDownloadShortBodyLeavesNothing asserts a non-zero exit saying the download stopped short and an empty folder, which is the whole reason for the temporary name. TestDownloadWontOverwrite asserts exit 2 with the existing file untouched, then that --force replaces it. TestDownloadOutsideWorkspaceRefused covers a folder outside the course and a link inside it pointing out, both exit 9 with nothing asked of Canvas. TestDownloadDisplayNameCantEscape asserts a display_name of ../../evil.sh saves as evil.sh inside the folder. TestDownloadRefusesANameThatIsntOne covers the display names that leave nothing to save under, "", ".", ".." and "/", each exit 2 with nothing saved. TestDownloadNormalModeNeedsCourse asserts --course is required outside Canvas Builder, exit 2, with nothing asked of Canvas.

CodeRabbit reviewed the patch and raised two findings, both minor and both valid, both fixed. The first: a trailing separator on --output was documented as naming a folder whether or not it existed, and nothing created it, so --output newdir/ failed at the temporary file with a message that didn't say the folder was missing. The folder is now required, with exit 2 naming it; creating it was rejected because a typo in an agent's path would otherwise leave a folder named after the typo in the instructor's course workspace. TestDownloadWontInventAFolder covers it. The second: --dry-run makes the client answer {"dry_run": true} without sending, which DownloadFile read as a file record with no file and reported as the course answering without naming the file, after the command had already created a temporary file. The client now returns ErrDryRun at that point and the command stops there, printing the generated commands' dry-run envelope shape, with the request preview the client prints still intact and nothing written. TestDownloadDryRunSavesNothing covers it.
